I'm sorry to hear that you lost your job today. Losing a job can be a difficult and stressful experience, especially when it comes unexpectedly. It's understandable that you might be feeling a range of emotions right now, such as sadness, frustration, or even anger.

It's important to remember that you are not alone in this situation, and that many people have gone through something similar. While it may be difficult to see the bright side right now, try to focus on the fact that you have experience and skills that are valuable in the job market.

In the meantime, take some time to reflect on what you have learned from your previous job and what you would like to do in the future. This can help you to gain clarity on your career path and make informed decisions about your next steps.

It may also be helpful to reach out to friends, family, or a professional career counselor for support and guidance. They may be able to provide you with resources or advice to help you navigate this difficult time.

Remember, it's okay to take time to grieve the loss of your job and to process your emotions. But don't lose hope, and keep an open mind to new opportunities that may come your way

I'm sorry to hear that your best friend hasn't been in touch with you. It can be difficult to understand why someone might stop talking to you, but it's important to remember that there may be reasons that are not necessarily related to you.

One thing you can do is to try to reach out to your friend and let them know that you're thinking about them. You could send them a message or call them to see how they're doing. It's possible that they're going through a difficult time and could use a friendly voice to talk to.

Another thing you can do is to give them space if they seem to want it. Sometimes people need time to process their emotions or figure out what they want to say.

It's also possible that there was something that happened that caused a rift between you two, and it's up to them to communicate that to you. In any case, it's important to be patient and understanding, and to give them the time and space they need.

They can help you develop coping strategies to manage your anxiety and improve your overall well-being.
